analysis.investment_thesis: Corona Remedies is a quality pharma formulations fast-grower with exceptional gross margins (80.8%) and ROCE (31.5%), but at P/E 62x the PEG ratio clocks in at ~1.9x even using the impressive 2-year earnings CAGR of 32% — that's too rich for my taste. I'd love this story at half the price; right now the market has already priced in most of the growth.
key_strengths: Exceptional gross margin of 80.8% signals premium branded formulations with real pricing power — classic pharma moat
Balance sheet cleaned up beautifully: D/E collapsed from 0.31 to 0.10, and OCF hit ₹190 Cr with FCF turning positive at ₹99 Cr in FY25
Operating margin nearly doubled from 14.5% to 20.1% in two years — FY25 earnings jumped 65.6% — this margin re-rating is the real story
key_risks: PEG ~1.9x (P/E 62 ÷ 32% 2Y earnings CAGR) — overvalued for Lynch's GARP discipline; even forward PEG of ~1.2x offers thin margin of safety
The FY25 profit surge (+65.6%) was driven heavily by margin expansion, not just revenue growth (+17.9%) — if margins mean-revert, the earnings story collapses fast
CWIP ballooning to ₹205 Cr (up from ₹65 Cr) signals another heavy capex cycle ahead — FY24 already produced ₹286 Cr capex and negative FCF of -₹129 Cr
red_flags: PEG ratio exceeds 1.5x threshold — Lynch red flag
Low FII ownership (1.84%) and missing market cap data makes liquidity and institutional interest hard to assess
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Corona Remedies is the kind of story I'd find walking the aisles of a pharmacy — women's health, cardio-diabetes, pain management, thyroid — all high-growth Indian therapeutic segments with demographic tailwinds. Revenue compounded at ~16% over two years (₹884 Cr → ₹1,196 Cr), but the real headline is the operating margin leap from 14.5% to 20.1% between FY23 and FY25, which turbocharged net profit from ₹85 Cr to ₹149 Cr (+75% cumulative). ROCE of 31.5% and ROE of 27.6% are hallmarks of a genuinely good business, not financial engineering.

The problem is simple: the market knows all of this. At P/E 62x, you're paying a steep premium for a ₹1,200 Cr revenue company. My PEG using the 2-year earnings CAGR of ~32% comes to 1.94 — well above my comfort zone of 1.0. Even on forward P/E of 40x, you need 35%+ sustained earnings growth to justify the price, and that margin expansion (the key driver) is unlikely to repeat at the same magnitude. The growing CWIP of ₹205 Cr also signals capacity investment that may temporarily pressure FCF again, much like FY24's -₹129 Cr FCF. I'd put this on my watchlist and revisit at a forward P/E closer to 25-28x.
